_meta.project: instex Instrument Explorer -- TELESCOPES mode: Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT, under construction) -- every focal station and the entrance pupil
_meta.companion: data/telescopes/gmt.md (same content as Markdown). Structure follows keck.json / magellan.json for a single telescope: sources{key: cite, file, url}; gmt: title, telescope (machine-readable primary, pupil, foci list; refs point to sourced params as 'gmt.<param>'), params, not_found, conflicts, notes.
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/telescopes/gmt/. derived = arithmetic done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). figure_readoff = a value read off a saved figure (its caption or a nearby text quote is checked). NOT FOUND marks a gap. Nothing is filled from memory.
_meta.quote_normalisation: Unicode NFKC; curly quotes, primes, dashes, minus, multiplication sign (to x), division slash, tilde operator, middle dot, the degree sign and the white-bullet degree glyph (U+25E6) normalised; whitespace collapsed; a quote also passes against the text with PDF line-end hyphenation removed or closed up, or with all whitespace removed; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces.
_meta.texts_checked: pdftotext -layout and -raw per page (PDF p. = page index of the saved PDF; for the GMT OAD this equals the printed 'Page N of 262'), tag-stripped text and raw source for HTML (UTF-8), .py and .md as is
_meta.pupil_frame: hcipy make_gmt_aperture frame (metres in the entrance pupil, angles from +x); orientation relative to the elevation axis NOT FOUND
_meta.design_vs_asbuilt: OAD Rev. G (2021) = current architecture; ORD Rev. E (2021) = requirements; CoDR (2006) = conceptual design; SB18, F22, B14 = GMTO overviews; hcipy = third-party pupil model
_meta.check_result: 134 quotes checked against the saved files, 0 failures (2026-10-19)

alternatives.quote: All FP/AP/IP instruments currently envisioned have a scientific field of view <30 arcsec. However, a technical field of view ≥ 2 arcmin is required to pass the natural and laser guide stars required to implement the NGAO and LTAO wavefront control modes.
The M3 shall provide a mechanism to rotate M3 about the Reference Optical Axis (ROA) and direct the Folded Gregorian beam to the Folded Port, Auxiliary Port, and Instrument Platform focal stations.
The M3 shall vignette no more than 48% of the 20 arcmin diameter Direct Gregorian field when deployed.
The specified M3 volume leaves 52% of the Direct Gregorian field unvignetted (82% of the annular field of view outside of 5.9 arcmin radius).
M3 must be removed from the Direct Gregorian optical path to enable the DGNF and DGWF optical layouts.

ap_station.quote: While the GMT does not have Nasmyth platforms, the Auxiliary Ports provide a similar gravity-invariant capability for narrow-field instruments. A mounting interface, utilities, and a volume are provided for two instruments on the elevation axis on the outboard side of both C-Rings.

alternatives.quote: An optical relay approximately 5 m in length is required to transfer the focal plane to the AP instrument volume.

The GMT also provides two auxiliary ports located outside the elevation bearings that accommodate smaller gravity-invariant instruments fed by an optical relay, such as high-contrast adaptive optics imagers.

conflicts: Plate scale: 0.994"/mm (OAD; 206264.8/207589 = 0.9936 DERIVED) vs 0.997"/mm (SB18 Table 1-1) vs 0.99"/mm at 'f/8.2' (B14) vs '1 arcsec/mm' (F22) and '1.0 mm per arcsecond' (SB18 text).

Primary focal length: the OAD text says the segments have 'a focal length of 36,000 mm', but 36 m is the radius of curvature (OAD Sec. 4.2.2; CoDR R1 = 36.000 m); CoDR: '18.0 meter primary mirror focal length'; f/0.71 x 25.4 m = 18.0 m. 18 m adopted.
Final focus: f/8.16, 207.589 m, 5.83 m below the M1 vertex (OAD 2021) vs f/8.0, 202.745 m, 5.50 m (CoDR 2006).
M2 segment diameter: 1.05 m (OAD, SB18, B14) vs 1.063 m (CoDR 2006) vs '1.1 m' (F22 Fig. 1 caption).
Central obscuration: 3.6 m M2 baffle (OAD 2021) vs 3.2 m baffle (CoDR 2006) vs 3.495 m hole (hcipy).

Collecting area: 368 m^2 (SB18, CoDR with the 3.2 m baffle) vs 375.558 m^2 geometric (OAD) vs >= 358 m^2 (OAD REQ-L3-OAD-63344) vs >= 356 m^2 (ORD REQ-L2-ORD-106537, also the OAD Table 4-29 margin note) vs 357.008 m^2 current best estimate (OAD Table 4-29) vs 358.48 m^2 (hcipy raster, DERIVED).
Site altitude: 2,550 m (F22 2022) vs 2518 m leveled summit (B14 2014) vs 2415 m leveled platform (OAD 2021).
C-ADC wavelength range: 350 nm to 1.0 um (OAD Sec. 3.1.2 text) vs 0.350 to 1.3 um (OAD Table 3-1 and REQ-L3-OAD-33875).
DG stations: 'four stations at the direct Gregorian focus inside the GIR' (SB18) vs three stored DG instruments plus the deployed bay (OAD Sec. 3.1.3, REQ-L3-OAD-69511).
ASM face sheets: holes at each segment centre (B14 2014, visible in the pupil) vs continuous face sheets (OAD 2021 Table 4-29).
M2 conjugation: 165 m above M1 (OAD) vs ~160 m above the ground (SB18, CoDR).
Segment gaps: 359 / 295 mm physical (CoDR 2006) vs 0.408 / 0.349 m between clear apertures (DERIVED from OAD numbers) vs 0.447 m (hcipy centre-to-off-axis) vs '> 30 cm' (HE22) vs '~30-100 cm' (K24).

Every Gregorian focus shares one pupil (M2 is the conjugate of M1 segment by segment); M3 and the C-ADC sit after the focus/below M1 and add no pupil obstruction in these sources.
